assessment.security_status_en: The security situation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab remains highly critical, as evidenced by the recent interception of a ballistic missile near a Belgian minehunter. Despite emerging diplomatic efforts toward a peace settlement in the Persian Gulf, attacks on oil tankers and military vessels persist.

recommendations.reason_en: Persistent attack risks in the Bab al-Mandab area keep shipping routes diverted around Africa, supporting freight rates but increasing operational uncertainty.

articles.title: Gulf states working on multipart peace deal to avert renewal of US-Iran war
articles.summary:
Talks are aimed at reopening strait of Hormuz and lifting sanctions on Iran, and for Houthis to withdraw in Yemen

A multipronged peace deal to reopen the strait of Hormuz within four days of sanctions being lifted and for the Houthis to withdraw substantial forces inside Yemen are at the heart of Gulf states’ plans to avert what they regard as a disastrous renewal of war between Iran and the US.

The US is aware of the talks’ progress but is holding out for a concession that European powers suggest could involve Iran allowing UN weapons inspectors back into the country.

articles.title: Trump says government to ‘terminate’ Biden-era methane emissions rules
articles.summary:
Critics warn of climate danger as president in Texas claims change will save companies and consumers billions

Donald Trump announced his administration is “terminating” Biden-era regulations holding oil and gas companies accountable for large leaks of planet-warming methane during a rally in Lubbock, Texas, on Tuesday evening.

Trump said during a campaign rally in Texas that the change would save consumers and energy producers $45bn and unlock 210 million barrels of oil – equivalent to about 10 days of US petroleum consumption. “Tonight, I’m officially terminating Biden’s expensive and unnecessary methane regulations to save consumers and energy producers,” Trump said, lifting what he called “crippling regulations on methane that caused prices to skyrocket” for small oil and gas operators.

articles.title: Eisenkot says Israel has chosen change, wants to form government
articles.summary:
Eisenkot says Israel has chosen change, wants to form government

Opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot said early Wednesday that Israel had chosen change after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and that he would seek to form a new government.

In remarks to supporters, Eisenkot also warned Netanyahu: "Don't you dare use Israel's security for your political needs," in a likely reference to his threats of new strikes on Iran.

He also said that he does not want a second election.

“In these elections, where there was a high percentage of Voters, it will be a mistake to rerun elections. It is my duty and the duties of everyone to be able to make the will of the people, a reality,” he said.

articles.summary:
Two men charged under National Security Act were directed by handler believed to have been working for Iranian intelligence, court told

A group of men were directed to drive vans loaded with petrol to Fairford RAF base by a handler known as Ali, who police believe was working on behalf of Iran, a court heard on Tuesday.

One of the five men tasked with driving to the base called police in the early hours of 27 September after the handler warned the group about a bomb in the vans, prosecutors told Westminster magistrates court.
